answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, select players+1 face-down without looking and return others; place one token on each of 11 marked territories; randomly select a structure bonus tile face-up below Popularity Track. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards; encounter tokens; structure bonus; starting player.

answers.answer: Place character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits in bottom circles; remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat; faction one-time spaces empty. Faction Mat sets power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and two objectives.

You may take neither action (dead turn), but must move token to a different section. Only Rusviet may repeat a section (including Factory); top and bottom each at most once. Top gains can pay bottom cost. Full exposed red-box cost is paid first; then choose as much or little green benefit as desired; top precedes bottom.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section; costs and benefits.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action costs from any territories you currently control, even elsewhere.

No: normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each. A transported worker may subsequently move itself. All unit types may carry any amount of resources; only mechs carry your workers, not your character.
answers.evidence: Top-row Move: two different units; carrying.

answers.answer: The character/mech enters and stops, cannot move again that turn; enemy workers retreat home leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker down to zero, but insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot enter independently while enemy workers control it.

Finish moving units, then resolve all combat before bottom-row action; attacker chooses order of multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

Bolster costs $1 for two power OR one combat card; if draw deck is empty shuffle discards; if both empty draw none. Trade costs $1 for any two resources OR one popularity. Traded resources go on controlled territory with at least one worker; cannot Trade resources if all workers home. Armory adds one power to Trade.

Pay all exposed Produce power/popularity/coin costs in full before production. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token. New workers come left-to-right from Player Mat into producing village. Production may be declined; new workers do not alter cost already paid, only future Produce costs.

Upgrade costs exposed Upgrade oil boxes; Deploy costs exposed Deploy metal boxes; amounts vary by mat/upgrades. Upgrade moves a cube from green box to empty bracketed red box to improve top benefit/reduce bottom cost. Deploy places chosen mech on controlled territory with your worker, never lake; ability then applies to character/all mechs, not workers. You may still pay completed bottom action for coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build on controlled territory with your worker; Factory allowed, lake/home base forbidden, and only one structure of any player per territory. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. Mill works only while you control its territory; Mine remains your personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled. Opponents cannot use your building abilities.

Put recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus space on Faction Mat: immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Ongoing bonus corresponds to circle uncovered where recruit was removed. On triggered action resolve active player, then left, then right; two-player opponent triggers once. Stop if sixth star ends game.

Each simultaneously/secretly selects dial power 0 through min(7,current power), then may add up to one card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers present); workers alone never fight. If both have mech abilities attacker uses first, then defender. Reveal together; add dial and card values, attacker wins ties. Both lose selected dial power; played cards are discarded face-up, with no track deduction for their value.

Winner controls territory/resources; losing characters, mechs, workers retreat to own home base leaving all resources (Nordic Seaworthy can retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes). Non-Saxony winner with zero/one combat star places one; with two places none; Saxony places after every victory while tokens available. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; defender loses none; Camaraderie exception applies. Loser draws one card if revealed any power by dial or cards; zero-total loser gets none.

After all combats, if character remains at encounter, discard token/draw card before following bottom action. If loses contested entry it retreats and token remains. Gains go on encounter territory. No additional normal action cost or mat benefit/recruit bonus.

Every player's character chooses one Factory card on first finish of Move there, after winning combat if needed; return rest. One permanent card each; later visits cannot choose/exchange. Factory card is fifth section, optional top then bottom and usual no-repeat (Rusviet exception); no matching mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Factory bottom moves one unit up to two territories, or three if character/mech with Speed; normal movement rules apply.

On your own turn before or after a top/bottom action, reveal completed objective only if all requirements met then; may wait. Place star and put both objective cards on bottom of deck. Normally one objective star; Saxony keeps second and can score both.

Stars for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two), 18 popularity, or 16 power; each once except combat two/Saxony exception. Others' stars do not block; stars cannot be lost. Sixth star immediately ends game.

For sixth star from bottom action, collect primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing star. Neighbor recruit star sequence: finish action, active player, left, right; check sixth star at each, then later bonuses/stars do not resolve. Pending intermingled battle: undo that part of movement, return initiating units; do not resolve another combat.

At 10 popularity, 5 stars yield $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as 7, yielding $21; 13 resources make 6 complete pairs, yielding $12. Thus $53 income is added to held coins and selected structure-tile bonus. Structures qualify even if enemies control their territories. Ties: workers+mechs+structures, power, popularity, controlled resources, territories, stars.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: popularity table, territory counts, structure eligibility and tiebreaks.

answers.answer: Home base is not a territory. Normally cannot move into any home base; setup/forced retreat exceptions, plus Crimea unlocked Wayfare. Expansion bases without matching core factions are inactive placeholders.
Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village worker; lake/Factory nothing. Workers are not resources. Supply has no resource-token limit; use multipliers if needed.

All units may pick/drop resources mid-movement; mech can also pick/drop carried workers mid-movement. Mechs never carry character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not workers; tunnel jump costs one step, extra step may be before/after; enemy/encounter stops override Speed.
Yes, any unit may enter enemy-structure-only territory, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: Enemy structure only; printed tunnels.

answers.answer: Do not pay partial cost. Since last section was Move, move token to another section and take neither action (dead turn) if unable to afford any action.

Armory grants +1 power on Trade; Monument grants +1 popularity on Bolster. These building benefits trigger on those actions and are retained even without control, except Mill production; enemy occupants do not gain building abilities.

Riverwalk applies to character and all mechs, not workers: Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic Swim is workers crossing rivers to land terrain, not lakes; distinct from Nordic mech Riverwalk.

Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move. Workers cannot use either shortcut.

Saxony Disarm: before combat on tunnel or own Mine, opponent loses two power on track once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery: before combat may pay one power to reduce opponent's power by two, once per combat, not per unit.
Two mechs and three workers allow three cards total with People's Army. Workers alone never fight; combat requires character/mech.

Crimea character/mechs may move from territory or home base to own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases; cannot enter active opponent home base.

Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion spends one combat card once per turn as any one resource regardless of card value.

Nordic Seaworthy permits character/mechs to/from lakes and retreat to adjacent lake; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge permits character/mechs to/from lakes and between any lakes, but no adjacent-lake retreat exception. Workers on lakes need mech to move off; cannot leave carried workers or resources behind when carrier leaves.
Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after winning combat as aggressor on your turn. Does not cover driving out undefended workers without combat.
Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.
Character stops upon entering encounter and cannot move further. Encounter resolves only after whole Move and all combats, if character remains there; same during Factory Move.

Combat hand count public, but whether cards committed may be concealed until reveal and contents secret until revealed. Objectives secret until reveal completed. Coins not hidden but exact total need not be stated when asked.

Agreements informal and unenforceable; coins are only tangible items exchangeable (tournament exception disallows even deal/alliance coin exchanges). Payment cannot cancel combat initiated by unit movement; bribes may influence outcome.
Popularity 0–6: $3/star, $2/territory, $1/per resource pair; 7–12: $4,$3,$2; 13–18: $5,$4,$3. Controlled lakes count, home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs count; odd token ignored.

Unique features count once across structures; adjacency unaffected by rivers. Tunnels adjacent to structures exclude Mines: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9. Encounters count unique printed locations even if token removed: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Lakes adjacent: unique lakes, same tiers through 4–5, then 6–7=$9. Zero scores $0.

Structures on printed tunnel territories (not Mines): 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Row counts only longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Farm/tundra structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on lake.
Star is permanent but current popularity determines final scoring tier. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions can both achieve/star same achievement.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Polania, Saxony clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Immediate left/right neighbors matter for recruit bonuses.

River is border between two land territories; lake occupies entire hex and extends to adjacent shoreline. Unit with applicable lake ability can enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No: show card to all players, show artwork and read capitalized thematic text aloud; every option need not be read aloud.
No limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

Next clockwise player may begin turn after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while current player decides upgrade/mech/structure/recruit to gain. Resolve interactive bonuses and end-game priority in order.
No. Chosen top and bottom actions each limited once within turn, even Rusviet; Rusviet exception only waives previous-turn section restriction.
Gain $1 instead of moving units.
No. Workers never return to Player Mat; this includes after retreat, since retreat sends them to home base.
Yes, may attack with zero power/popularity.
Yes, may continue fighting; after two combat stars non-Saxony winner places no further combat star.
Without Meander must choose one affordable option; cannot decline all or choose unaffordable coin/popularity options. May take as little of chosen benefit as desired.
Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, then optional cards; reveal simultaneously.
Announce bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
Star is placed as soon as goal achieved; sixth ends game immediately. Objective differs: completed objective may be held and revealed later, but at reveal all conditions must still be met.
No. Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes absent applicable faction/mech ability.
No. Recruit is placed permanently and cannot later move.
No. Only a character triggers encounter; character stops upon entering and encounter resolved after Move and combats if remains.

Controlled Mill adds one bonus territory to Produce allowance: normal two becomes up to three (upgraded three becomes four). Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces terrain token even with no actual worker; each actual worker there also produces normally. Mill works only while controlled.
Control requires your unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not preserve control after last unit leaves absent structure.
Build uses wood; Enlist uses food.
answers.evidence: Bottom resources: Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.
